questions.question: The 0.33 fixes made on master since the tag (BUG-280, BUG-298, BUG-330, BUG-333, and the breaking BK-405 and BUG-329): what happens to them when src/ goes back to v0.33.0?

options.label: Re-apply non-breaking (Recommended)
options.description: Port BUG-280, BUG-298, BUG-330 and BUG-333 onto the 0.33.0 code. They are real defects in released code (RFC-0024 class K). BK-405 and BUG-329, both Breaking, go to the frozen branch and come back as v1 break records later.

options.label: Re-apply all six
options.description: Also port the two breaking changes. Master's code is then 0.33.0 plus two behaviour breaks, which can't ship in a 0.33 patch.

options.label: Freeze them too
options.description: src/ is exactly v0.33.0. Every fix waits on the frozen branch, and the 0.33 line keeps known defects.

questions.question: Spec 054's number, given that 'spec 052' already means backend lifetime in RFC-0024, ADRs, traces and decision logs?

options.label: Keep 054, retire 052/053
options.description: 052 and 053 leave master. A short register row (or tombstone) points to the frozen branch, so every record that says 'spec 052' still resolves. No number changes meaning.

options.label: Renumber to 052 (as proposed)
options.description: 054 becomes 052 and the numbering stays dense. Records that cite 'spec 052' or BE-020 in 052 now point at the key spec; we'd add a note in the ground register's ID map.

options.label: Separate v1 numbering
options.description: Ground specs get their own sequence or prefix (e.g. V1-001 store tree, V1-002 key), so v1 and 0.33 specs can't be confused. 051 would be renamed too, which is a ground change (reopen).

options.label: Keep the branch
options.description: Keep RFC-0024's split as is. Master and the branch carry nearly identical code, so every fix costs a cherry-pick.

What carries the decision before any code moves?

options.label: RFC-0025 amending 0024 (Recommended)
options.description: A short RFC amends RFC-0024 R2 (pause and freeze), D2, D9 and D10 (now 'when the frozen branch is revived or rewritten'), and sets 'implementation frozen on a branch' as the status of RFC-0017, ADR-0042 and ADR-0047. The revert PRs then cite it. Costs one RFC review cycle first.

options.label: Amend RFC-0024 in place
options.description: Edit RFC-0024 itself, since it was accepted only yesterday. Fewer documents, but an accepted RFC gets rewritten rather than amended, against the repo's record rules.

options.label: Just do it, record after
options.description: Snapshot and revert now, writing the rationale into the revert PR and a trace. Fastest, but for a while the repo contradicts RFC-0024's text.

questions.question: How is the revert split into PRs?

options.label: Three PRs (Recommended)
options.description: (1) RFC-0025 plus the snapshot branch. (2) The revert: src/, tests, kernel specs, formal models, tooling, docs, CHANGELOG and backlog, with the four fixes re-applied, kept reviewable by splitting it into commits per area. (3) #1171 rebased: 054 renamed to 052 after 052 leaves master.

options.label: One big PR
options.description: Everything in one PR. Atomic, so the repo is never half-reverted, but it's a huge review, and a trace with mixed concerns.

options.label: Fold into #1171
options.description: Put the revert into the open spec 054 PR. Fewest PRs, but it mixes a new spec with a repo-wide revert, and the review loses focus.

questions.question: What happens to the open backlog items about kernel, driver or migration work (RFC-0024 class P, e.g. BK-450, BK-455, BK-452, ID-140, ID-181)?

options.label: Park in one dossier (Recommended)
options.description: Each item leaves BACKLOG.md as 'absorbed' into one host item ('Revive or rewrite the frozen kernel line', the new D10). Its dossier lists every parked ID with a one-line diagnosis and points to the branch. The index shrinks and nothing is lost.

options.label: Keep them open, tagged
options.description: Each stays in its section with 'frozen (RFC-0025)' in its entry. They stay visible but clutter the index and inflate the open count.

options.label: Decide against them all
options.description: Close them as decided against, since a rewrite will re-derive them from the v1 specs. Cleanest, but it records a verdict you haven't reached item by item.

options.label: Keep on master
options.description: It stays as a second formal view of 051. Its kernel-encoding parts then cite a spec (053) that's no longer on master.

Spec 051 (ground) says in its non-normative Layering paragraph that spec 053's BE-032 encodes the tree. 053 leaves master. How does RFC-0025 handle that, given RFC-0024's 'nothing changes ground on the side'?

options.label: Rule: pointers aren't ground (Recommended)
options.description: RFC-0025 rules that editing a pointer to another spec in a ground spec's non-normative paragraph is not a change to ground, and the register records the rule. PR 2 then drops the 053 sentence, and PR 3 repoints '004' to the new 052. This also settles BK-487's open decision, which is the same question.

options.label: Recorded reopen of 051
options.description: A reopen decision for spec 051 that runs its own small flow, with the register flagging 051 'reopened' meanwhile. Strict to the letter of RFC-0024, but /observe sessions lose 051 as ground until the reopen closes.

options.label: Leave it, note it
options.description: Leave the paragraph untouched and record in the register that it cites a frozen spec. Ground stays byte-identical, but a ground spec points to something no session can read.

questions.question: RFC-0024's class P list mixes kernel work with 0.33 work. How does D7 split them?

options.label: Absorb kernel only (Recommended)
options.description: BK-450, BK-455, BK-452, BK-439, BK-446, BK-390 and BK-434 are absorbed into the D10 host item. ID-140 and ID-181 stay open as 0.33 features. They're minor bumps, so under D5 they wait for v1 flows; their 'paused (RFC-0024)' notes are updated. BK-345 stays open as a 0.33 conformance gate (with ID-244).

options.label: Absorb all ten
options.description: Keep D7 as drafted. Simpler, but three 0.33 items end up under 'revive the kernel'.

questions.question: Spec 051's Layering paragraph points at specs 004 and 053, and neither is the right owner once RFC-0025 lands. How does RFC-0025 handle a pointer in ground spec 051 that the freeze breaks?

options.label: Rule: pointers aren't ground (Recommended)
options.description: RFC-0025 rules that changing a cross-spec pointer in a ground spec's non-normative paragraph (Layering, Tested against) does not change ground, so no reopen is needed. PR 2 drops the 053 sentence, PR 3 points input strings at spec 052 (the key spec), and BK-487 closes on that ruling. The ground register records the edit.

options.label: Recorded reopen of 051
options.description: Treat it as a change to ground. Record a reopen decision, run 051 through its own small flow and re-admit it. Strict, but it's process overhead for a two-sentence pointer.

options.label: Leave it stale
options.description: Spec 051 keeps pointing at 053 and 004 until v1 flows rework it. Nothing changes in ground, but a ground spec then cites a spec that isn't on master.
